passage: On the tram in Prague, Jana said she would be up at six to revise for tomorrow's test. Camila arched one eyebrow slowly. "You? At six?" Jana burst into laughter. "Okay, okay, seven!" They had done this dozens of times. The eyebrow meant, of course you will. But at the next stop, Nadia, a new girl who had joined their table that week, said she planned to try out for the school choir. Camila raised the same eyebrow, and Nadia went stiff and looked at her shoes. Jana leaned over quickly. "Camila, it is banter, she does not know you yet," and Camila said, "Sorry, Nadia. That was a joke, I think you will get in."

qa.a: Jana said she would be up at six to revise.

qa.q: What did Nadia feel when Camila raised an eyebrow at her?
qa.a: She stiffened and looked at her shoes, so she probably felt unsure or stung, since she did not know Camila's joking style yet. She might also have been simply shy.

qa.a: Camila apologised, said the eyebrow was a joke and told Nadia, "I think you will get in."

qa.q: How does the same eyebrow look different to Jana than to Nadia?
qa.a: For Jana it is a known joke from many past laughs, while for Nadia, who is new, it could look like doubt or mockery.

I'm sorry about Thursday. When you said you'd read the whole novel in one weekend, I did my one-eyebrow thing and said, "Oh really?" I meant it as a joke, like when we tease each other about who eats the most samosas.

Friends?
Usha

"Rehana, you want to know my secret at chess club? It's my eyebrow.
When someone says, 'I'll checkmate you in five moves,' I raise one eyebrow, like this, and say, 'Oh, really?' It's my way of saying, 'Challenge accepted.' Everyone in club knows it. They laugh and raise theirs back.
But last week a new girl joined. I did the eyebrow when she said she'd played in a tournament. Her face went red, and she didn't talk for the rest of the session.
I felt terrible. She didn't know it was a joke. The next day I told her, 'That eyebrow means I'm excited to play you, not that I don't believe you.'
She laughed and raised her own eyebrow back. So now I, Keerthana, explain the eyebrow to every new member."

qa.q: What does Keerthana's eyebrow raise mean at chess club?
qa.a: "Challenge accepted."

qa.q: What was the new girl feeling when her face went red?
qa.a: She probably felt embarrassed and hurt, thinking Keerthana doubted her tournament story.

qa.q: What did Keerthana do to fix the misunderstanding?
qa.a: She explained the eyebrow's playful meaning the next day, and now tells every new member.

qa.q: How might the regular club members see the eyebrow raise?
qa.a: They see it as a playful challenge and enjoy raising theirs back.

grounding: A teenager explains a raised eyebrow as playful banter at chess club, and how it stung a newcomer who didn't know.

passage:
At dinner my sister Arohi and her friend Kavita were joking about who'd win the class quiz. Kavita said she'd win because she'd memorised all the capitals.
Arohi raised both eyebrows high, tilted her head and said, "Oh, reeeally?"
Kavita raised hers back even higher. "Yes, reeeally!" They both burst out laughing. I've seen them do this a hundred times.
Then Arohi turned to our cousin Meenal, who's new to the city, and raised an eyebrow when she said she liked cricket. Meenal's smile froze. She looked at her plate.
I couldn't tell if she was hurt or just shy. Arohi noticed too, and added quickly, "That means cool! You can join our team."
Meenal smiled again, a bit slowly.
- Akash

qa.q: What did Kavita say she had memorised?
qa.a: All the capitals.

qa.q: What might Meenal have been feeling when her smile froze?
qa.a: She may have felt unsure or hurt, not knowing if the raised eyebrow was friendly, though Akash couldn't tell if she was just shy.

qa.q: What did Arohi do that helped Meenal?
qa.a: She noticed the change and quickly explained the eyebrow meant "cool", inviting Meenal to join.

qa.q: How does Kavita see Arohi's eyebrow raise compared with Meenal?
qa.a: Kavita knows it's playful banter and raises hers back, while Meenal, being new, wasn't sure what it meant.

grounding: An observer sees eyebrow banter that friends read as playful, but which unsettles a newcomer until it is explained.
